pointers.concern: Unsafe reflection: setAccessible(true) called on arbitrary fields without validation
pointers.why: Bypasses Java access control on private fields. Combined with field traversal of all plugins, could leak sensitive data or allow access to fields of untrusted plugins

pointers.concern: Reflection traversal of arbitrary plugin object fields without trust boundary
pointers.why: The code iterates through getDeclaredFields() of any Plugin class and calls setAccessible(true), then accesses field values. No validation that the plugin is trusted before deep reflection

pointers.concern: Package name prefix matching used as security boundary
pointers.why: isOwnedType() only checks package.getName().startsWith(ownerPackage). A malicious plugin could use a similar package name (e.g. 'com.pathrender.memorydiagnostic.evil') to bypass the ownership check

pointers.concern: Reflection used on all enabled plugins without prior security check
pointers.why: updateUsage() calls estimator.estimate(plugin) on every plugin from pluginManager.getPlugins(). No verification that plugin is safe before invoking reflection traversal

pointers.concern: field.get(obj) called in loop with incomplete exception handling
pointers.why: Only catches IllegalAccessException. Other exceptions (NullPointerException, SecurityException) could occur and indicate unexpected field state or intentionally obfuscated fields
